hostHelp: Use a fixed IP address. Modbus TCP must be switched on at the Navigator (Settings → Building management → Modbus TCP = On).
requestPauseHelp: The Navigator stalls under hard polling - minimum 100 ms.
intervalFastHelp: Fast: outdoor temperature, power, heat pump status. Medium: storage and room temperatures. Slow: energy meters, solar, cascade. Minimum 10 s.
testNoHost: Please enter the Navigator host first
testConnectFailed: Connection failed - check host, port and that Modbus TCP is enabled on the Navigator
testReadFailed: Connected, but reading the outdoor temperature failed - check the unit ID
removeInactiveStates: Delete states of circuits, zones and blocks switched off here
removeInactiveStatesHelp: Deletes the states and channels of heating circuits, zones and blocks you switched off. Off by default.
scanHelp: Reads every register one by one (about 3 minutes, read requests only) and suggests the installation layout. Polling pauses meanwhile. Afterwards press "Apply suggestion" and save.
scanStarted: Scan started - it takes about %s minutes. Do not restart or reload the adapter meanwhile. The progress is in the state diag.scanProgress and the log, the result in the log and in the state diag.scan.
scanNoHost: Please enter the Navigator host first
scanFamilyUnavailable: There is no register file for this Navigator generation yet
intervalConfigHelp: How often adjustable settings (operating modes, setpoints, heating curves, limits) are read again. They change rarely and are also read at start. Minimum 60 s.
statsEnabledHelp: COP, annual performance factor, energy per operating mode, cost, CO₂, operating hours and starts. Read-only, nothing is written to the heat pump.
extElecHelp: A meter that measures the real electricity of the heat pump gives a second, independent COP. A cumulative counter is preferred (it keeps counting while the adapter is stopped); a power state alone is integrated. Make sure the meter measures only the heat pump.
thermalSource: Heat source for the efficiency figures
externalMaxAgeHelp: An older external power value is ignored for the momentary COP. Minimum 10 s.
resetStatsConfirm: Delete all statistics and start from zero?
unitHelp: Auto reads the unit of the state. If the state has no unit, choose it here; until then the source stays off. For other scales (for example a register in steps of 0.1 W) create an alias or a derived state in ioBroker that converts to W or kWh.
controlWarning: Everything is off by default. Only switch on what you need. Many settings are stored in the Navigator's EEPROM, which tolerates about 300,000 writes in its lifetime: never let an automation write them continuously. Every value is checked against the documented range, debounced and read back; writes to EEPROM settings are limited by the minimum interval below.
writeSystem: Allow writing: system mode and fault acknowledgement
writeExpert: Allow writing: bivalence and cascade (expert mode)
writeExpertHelp: Wrong values here change how the whole installation is laid out. Only for those who know what they are doing.
eepromMinIntervalS: Minimum time between two writes of one setting (s)
eepromMinIntervalHelp: Protects the EEPROM: a newer value waits until this time has passed. Minimum 10 s, recommended 60 s.
dailyWriteWarn: Warn above this many writes per setting and day
writeZones: Allow writing: room setpoints and operating modes (Navigator Pro)
writeZonesHelp: Only the setpoint (in steps of 0.5 °C) and the operating mode of each room; temperature and humidity stay read-only. A setpoint from here only takes effect while the room is in operating mode Normal. Do not write continuously: the zone module restarts.
pvEnabled: Send PV values to the Navigator
pvEnabledHelp: Writes the configured values cyclically to registers 74-86. Switch off any other program that writes them (a second writer is reported). The PV menu of the Navigator must be set up.
pvMaxAgeS: Maximum age of a source value (s)
pvMaxAgeHelp: Older values count as missing: the surplus is then written as 0, the other registers are not written.
pvModeHelp: Direct: the surplus row below is written as it is (a grid feed-in state works with a factor and Invert). Calculated: needs rows for PV production and house consumption; the surplus row only gives the limits.
pvSourcesHelp: One row per register. The factor converts the state's unit to kW (1 for kW, 0.001 for W) or percent. There is deliberately no default.
roomsEnabled: Send room temperatures to the Navigator
roomsEnabledHelp: Writes the temperature of a state to the external room temperature of a heating circuit (registers 1650 to 1662). In the Navigator the room must use the Modbus/GLT sensor as its temperature source.
roomSourcesHelp: One row per heating circuit. A change of at least the tolerance is written at once, otherwise at the heartbeat. Values outside min/max and old values are never written.
gltEnabled: Send building automation values to the Navigator
gltEnabledHelp: Writes outdoor temperature, humidity, demands and storage temperatures cyclically (registers 1690 to 1722). The matching GLT options must be switched on in the Navigator, for example "GLT outdoor temperature". Only switch on what the Navigator is set up to use.
gltSourcesHelp: One row per value. Empty heartbeat, minimum and maximum take the defaults of the value. Booleans: a state that is true or 1 means demand. Values outside the range and old values are never written.
blockBooster: Booster heat pumps A and B (Navigator 10)
testOkMismatch: Connection successful (outdoor temperature %s °C). Detected: %s, but %s is selected - change the Navigator generation.
testOkUnknown: Connection successful (outdoor temperature %s °C). The Navigator generation could not be detected.
webEnabled: Also read data from the web interface (inputs and outputs; Navigator 2.0 / Pro: also room names, room data and statistics)
webEnabledHelp: Read only. Uses the PIN of the display (same as the login in the browser). Navigator 2.0 / Pro: sets the names of rooms and heating circuits, adds rooms that Modbus does not read and the statistics of the Navigator. Navigator 10: reads the inputs and outputs through its WebSocket. Parts that Modbus delivers are not created from the web interface. Not available for the Navigator 1.0/1.7. The web interface is not documented by IDM and may change with firmware updates. The PIN is sent unencrypted in your local network, like in the browser.
webStatisticsHelp: Reads runtime, heat quantity and electrical energy (today, month, year, total, history back to the start) and calculates the COP from them.
prereqText: Before the first start: Modbus TCP is switched off by default and has to be enabled on the Navigator once: in the main menu "Settings" choose "Building management" (Gebäudeleittechnik) and set "Modbus TCP" to "On" (installer or service level, so ask your installer if you cannot see it). Use a fixed IP address for the Navigator.
webPrereq: The web interface needs the network PIN of the Navigator. If you do not know it or none is set, it has to be set up on the Navigator first (usually at installer level, ask your installer). Modbus TCP and the web interface are enabled separately; the adapter works without the web interface.
boostEnabled: Allow the one-time hot water boost
boostEnabledHelp: Creates the buttons dhw.boost_start and dhw.boost_stop. A boost switches on the hot water demand of the Navigator (register 1712) and refreshes it every 30 s. The adapter always switches it off again: at the target temperature, after the time limit, on request, after three failed writes, when it stops and after a restart. Without that the Navigator would keep charging, because this demand does not stop at the storage temperature.
hideUnavailable: Hide states of hardware that reports no value
hideUnavailableHelp: Hardware your plant does not have (sensors, pumps, solar, ...) is reported as "not available" and would only show empty values. With this option such states are not created, and those left over from earlier starts are removed about two minutes after the start. A state appears by itself as soon as the Navigator reports a real value. Custom settings of a removed state (for example history) are lost.
scanResult: Scan of %s: %s registers answered, %s answered "not available", %s do not exist. Suggested installation: heating circuits %s, zone modules %s (rooms per module %s), blocks %s.
scanNone: No scan result yet - start a scan first
scanApplied: Taken over into the form: heating circuits %s, zone modules %s, blocks %s. Check it and save the settings.
co2StateHelp: State with the current CO₂ intensity of your electricity in the unit chosen next to the fixed CO₂ factor, for example from a grid or tariff adapter. The emissions are accrued with the value valid when the energy was used. While the state has no value, the fixed value is used.
supportHelp: Creates a report for bug reports: the configuration without host, PIN and state ids, the connection state, registers that report no value, the latest readings of all registers and the result of the last scan. IP addresses and e-mail addresses are removed. The file opens in a new tab and stays in the file area support; attach it to your bug report together with the adapter log.
supportCreated: Support file %s created. It opens in a new tab.
supportFailed: The support file could not be created - see the log
diagramHiddenHelp: Choose parts that should not be drawn. Parts the heating system does not have are not drawn anyway.
webPortHelp: 0 = automatic: 80 for the Navigator 2.0 / Pro, 61220 (WebSocket) for the Navigator 10
diagramIntro: The diagram is a read-only web page that draws your heating system with live values. Open it with the link next to the instance in the instances list; it needs a web adapter instance. It builds itself from the values the adapter has. Use these settings when it guesses wrong or you want a simpler picture; they apply at once.
diagramHeatSourceHelp: Air heat pumps are drawn with a fan, ground and groundwater heat pumps with a source pump. Automatic decides from the sensors the Navigator reports.
diagramZoneCircuitHelp: By default the rooms of zone module 1 stand next to heating circuit A, those of module 2 next to circuit B, and so on. Add a row to place a zone module next to another circuit.
priceUnitHelp: How the fixed price and the price state are given.
co2UnitHelp: How the fixed CO₂ factor and the CO₂ state are given.
diagramCopHelp: One COP follows the source above; "Both" shows the Navigator COP and the external COP.
diagramSourceHelp: Electrical power, thermal power and COP come from the Navigator or from your external meters (Statistics tab). Where an external value is missing, the Navigator value is shown.
